newsitem.title: USA: Top U.S. tax legislator backs credit unions.
newsitem.headline: Top U.S. tax legislator backs credit unions.

text.p: Senate Finance Committee chairman William Roth strongly backed credit unions in their legal battle over membership limits and said he would fight to preserve their tax-exempt status.

The Supreme Court said on Monday it would hear an appeal of a six-year old lawsuit filed by banks seeking to curtail membership at credit unions, non-profit cooperatives that provide bank-like services.
Until 1982, a credit union's members had to share a single "common bond," such as working for the same employer or living in the same neighborhood.

But in 1982, the federal regulator of credit unions decided that a credit union could accept members from more than one group as long as each group was distinct. Banks filed suit in 1990 challenging the new interpretation.
Sen Roth, Republican of Delaware, said if the Supreme Court rules against credit unions, he would support legislation to permit broader membership.

"If the common bond is not resolved in your favor in the Supreme Court, then we can look to change the law to provide a better definition," Roth said in a speech here to the Credit Union National Association, a leading trade group.
The court is expected to hear arguments in the case in the fall with a decision expected early next year.
"This I believe would be a much better solution than eliminating the distinction between banks and credit uinions," Roth added.
Banks have argued that if credit unions are allowed to accept members from more than one group, then the non-profits should pay taxes, but Roth said he would oppose such a change.
"As chairman of the tax writing committee in the Senate, I will remain firm in my position that credit unions keep their tax exempt status," he said.
Roth also praised credit unions for serving consumers, a mission he said they should maintain even if they win in the Supreme Court.

"Let me say that if the definition of common bond is settled in your favor by a Supreme Court ruling, I hope that our credit unions focus on their traditional role, that's what they do best," Roth said. "For 13 straight years, credit unions have ranked as the top financial institutions when it comes to consumer satifaction."
